sections.title: History of Present Illness
sections.content: Mr. Brown is a 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension who presents today with complaints of frequent headaches over the past 3 months. He describes the headaches as bilateral, pressure-like, occurring 3-4 times per week, and lasting several hours. He denies visual changes, nausea, or vomiting. He reports stress at work and poor sleep quality. His blood glucose has been well controlled on current medications.

sections.title: Physical Exam
sections.content:
Vitals: BP 138/88 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, Temp 98.6°F, SpO2 98% on room air
General: Alert and oriented, no acute distress
HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic, pupils equal and reactive, no papilledema
Neck: Supple, no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended
Extremities: No edema, pulses 2+ bilaterally
Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, strength 5/5 throughout

sections.title: Results
sections.content:
Recent Labs (dated 10/15):
- HbA1c: 6.8% (improved from 7.2%)
- Fasting glucose: 118 mg/dL
- BMP: Within normal limits, Cr 0.9
- Lipid panel: Total cholesterol 195, LDL 110, HDL 52, TG 165
- CBC: WNL

EKG: Normal sinus rhythm, no ST changes

sections.title: Assessment & Plan
sections.content:
1. Tension-type headaches - likely related to stress and poor sleep
   - Recommend stress management techniques
   - Trial of OTC acetaminophen or ibuprofen as needed
   - Sleep hygiene counseling provided
   - Follow up if headaches worsen or change in character

2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - well controlled
   - Continue current regimen
   - HbA1c at goal

3. Hypertension - slightly elevated today
   - Continue current medications
   - Dietary counseling on sodium restriction
   - Recheck BP in 2 weeks
